claim: Singapore is a relevant setting for migrant-remittance research
statistic_or_finding: Total foreign workforce: 1,655,900; Work Permit holders: 1,243,600.
source_locator: June 2026 column; totals and Work Permit rows
relevance_to_project: Context for potential users, not a demand estimate
qualification_or_limit: Foreign workforce includes heterogeneous groups; not the number of remittance users or evidence of their transfer volumes or hardship.

claim: Real remittance provision has a regulated institutional context
statistic_or_finding: MAS identifies cross-border money transfer among regulated payment services; providers require a licence unless exempted.
source_locator: introductory licensing statement; cross-border money transfer row
relevance_to_project: Explains why a test workflow cannot replace regulated settlement
qualification_or_limit: Classification information, not legal advice or a determination of the prototype’s regulatory status.

claim: Some conventional Singapore corridors already support real-time transfers
source_organization: Monetary Authority of Singapore / Reserve Bank of India
source_title: Launch of Real-time Payments between Singapore and India
statistic_or_finding: PayNow–UPI launched real-time bank/e-wallet transfers for participating customers; announcement explicitly includes foreign workers and students in accessibility aims.
relevance_to_project: Supports relevance while contradicting universal-delay claims
qualification_or_limit: Launch capability and stated aim; not current adoption, universal eligibility, quantified user satisfaction or all-corridor performance.

claim: Global remittance costs remain above the policy benchmark
publication_date: 2025-09 (report label; exact release day not stated)
statistic_or_finding: Global average total cost for the USD 200 benchmark: 6.36% in Q3 2025.
source_locator: printed pp.6–7; global and digital/non-digital cost sections
relevance_to_project: Motivates cost as a contextual friction
qualification_or_limit: Surveyed-service benchmark, not a Singapore price, every corridor, or measured prototype savings; see E06.

publication_date: 2025-09 (report label; exact release day not stated)
statistic_or_finding: Digital average 4.59%; non-digital average 7.30% in Q3 2025.
source_locator: printed pp.6–7; global and digital/non-digital cost sections
relevance_to_project: Requires qualified rather than universal problem framing
qualification_or_limit: Descriptive channel comparison; not causal evidence that digitisation or blockchain causes the difference.

claim: The remittance cost benchmark has a specific measurement scope
data_period: methodology accessed October 2026; not a price observation
statistic_or_finding: RPW measures fees and exchange-rate margin using standardised survey amounts; prices are point-in-time snapshots.
source_locator: Amounts; Transfer fee; Exchange Rate Margin; disclaimer
qualification_or_limit: Local-currency price points need not equal today’s USD equivalent; some receiving fees/taxes and unavailable FX information are not captured.

claim: Remittance speed is uneven in the monitored market
source_title: G20 Roadmap for Cross-border Payments: Consolidated progress report for 2025
data_period: 2025 KPI column uses World Bank RPW Q1 2025
geography: global remittance services with disclosed speed
statistic_or_finding: 2025 KPI: 54.4% available within one hour; 76.3% within one business day.
source_locator: Table 17, printed p.58 / PDF page 62; table note
relevance_to_project: Supports speed variability without a universal settlement-delay claim
qualification_or_limit: Q1 2025 USD 200 services with end-user speed information only; percentages of services, not observed transactions or Singapore users.

claim: International policy targets recognise cost and information needs
source_title: Targets for addressing the four challenges of cross-border payments: Final report
data_period: policy targets for end-2027 and 2030; not outcomes
statistic_or_finding: Remittance cost target: global USD 200 average no more than 3% by 2030, no corridors above 5%. Transparency target includes charges, FX, expected delivery time and tracking.
source_locator: targets table; official G20 targets summary linked in research document
relevance_to_project: Benchmark plus rationale for visible lifecycle state
qualification_or_limit: Targets are ambitions, not achieved outcomes, law or evidence that the MVP satisfies them.

claim: Payment-chain structure can complicate cost and status transparency
source_title: Transparency in retail cross-border payments and remittances
publication_date: 2026-09 (publication listing; exact day not relied upon)
data_period: 2025–26 work programme; questionnaire and desk research; no single consumer reference period
statistic_or_finding: Multiple intermediaries complicate upfront cost disclosure; tracking depends on interoperability and information sharing.
source_locator: executive summary p.6; methodology pp.11–12; considerations/conclusions pp.41–42
qualification_or_limit: Policy/jurisdiction evidence, not measured prevalence among Singapore remittance users; on-chain status does not expose bank settlement.

claim: Operating-hour gaps can add cross-border payment friction
source_title: Changing the clock: practical approaches to extend payment system operating hours
data_period: jurisdictional operating-hours experiences reviewed for 2025 brief
statistic_or_finding: RTGS operating hours and time-zone overlap affect settlement opportunities.
qualification_or_limit: System-level analysis and author views, not a universal remittance delay or an estimate for Singapore migrants.

claim: Non-blockchain interlinking is a credible architectural alternative
geography: Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand; broader design
statistic_or_finding: Nexus proposes standardised connections between domestic instant payment systems.
relevance_to_project: Avoids claiming blockchain is the only way to improve cross-border payments
qualification_or_limit: 2024 blueprint; not proof of globally completed deployment or measured consumer savings.

claim: Public-chain designs have costs and dependencies
source_title: The crypto ecosystem: key elements and risks
statistic_or_finding: BIS analysis identifies congestion/fees, fragmentation and centralisation risks in crypto systems.
source_locator: overview: congestion, fees, fragmentation and centralisation risks
qualification_or_limit: Broad ecosystem analysis, not a fee forecast for Sepolia or proof that this MVP includes DeFi/stablecoins.

claim: Technical innovation does not alone resolve cross-border coordination
source_title: Cross-border payment technologies: innovations and challenges
data_period: technology and institutional analysis at publication
statistic_or_finding: Interoperability and institutional coordination remain constraints on payment improvements.
relevance_to_project: Explains why ledger transparency is only part of the solution
qualification_or_limit: Research synthesis, not a quantified access deficit for Singapore or a claim that wallets solve inclusion.
